Every G6B-parsed byte sequence must be rejected identically by G6C.

contract.instructions: Implement ProviderRequestContractV1, SearchCandidateForProviderV1, parseProviderRequestContractV1, and buildRankingProviderRequestV1 in packages/mcp/src/core/ranking-provider-request-v1.ts exactly per plan §6.4. The builder must canonicalize and hash the supplied contract itself, return that digest, and reject unless it equals expectedProviderRequestContractSha256; the returned digest must equal the canonical hash of the supplied contract AND the sealed R1.2 index digest — no caller recalculates the expected value (B9, E2, G2, G6B/H4, G6C/I2 import this implementation unchanged and receive the expected digest only from the sealed R1.2 training-contract index). First-RED test (plan §7.6): packages/mcp/src/core/ranking-provider-request-v1.test.ts — 'builder_hashes_contract_and_rejects_expected_digest_mismatch'; expected failure before implementation is that a structurally valid contract whose canonical digest differs from expectedProviderRequestContractSha256 is accepted; minimal passing behavior is that the returned contract digest equals the canonical supplied contract and must equal the sealed R1.2 digest. Tests must also cover exact identity/configuration matching to FixedProviderTargetV1, frozen baseline-admission order, and payload bounds. Do not modify the parent integration checkout. NOTE: the focused command is plan-specified (§7.5) and targets a future test file that does not exist at round_base — unverifiable-at-base; the affected command is repo-verified (packages/mcp/package.json test script exists) but cannot exercise A12 code until the file exists.
